perspective:
**Harold Padilla’s available information**

- Harold knows he is the project manager and knows Arthur Begum as a police officer/friend whose advice he seeks.
- Harold felt frustrated and anxious about the project’s progress and believed his team was unmotivated. He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- At that meeting, Harold told Arthur his team seemed completely unmotivated and was affecting progress. Arthur said motivation can be tricky and asked whether Harold had tried understanding what drives each team member individually. Harold admitted he had focused on goals and deadlines. Arthur advised one-on-one conversations and making people feel valued and understood. Harold said he would try it and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold felt hopeful and relieved and decided to use Arthur’s advice. In a team meeting, he proposed quick one-on-one chats to understand each member’s motivation. Team Member 1 said it could be helpful; Team Member 2 said they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time and urged the team to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried and spoke with Arthur again. Harold told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still was not responding. Arthur said there might be deeper team problems, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors. Harold said he would set up another round of meetings and thanked Arthur.
- Harold then held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns. Team Member 1 told him there was tension between a few team members affecting work. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and asked if there was anything else. Team Member 2 told him they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold said he understood, would see about redistributing tasks, and said their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered and believed addressing individual concerns would improve performance. He intended to create a more supportive, open team environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He told the team this. Team Member 1 said it sounded great and would help; Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad and emphasized working together and valuing input and well-being.

Harold does not have access to Arthur’s or the team members’ private thoughts beyond what they said or did in his presence.
